title: Maryland: history overview
d: Maryland: the Old Line State, admitted 1788 (7th); capital Annapolis.
definition: Maryland: the Old Line State, admitted 1788 (7th); capital Annapolis.
description: Maryland — "Old Line State" — entered the Union 1788 (7th). Its capital is Annapolis and its largest city is Baltimore. Catholic refuge colony 1634. This database tells the state's story: from its first peoples through statehood to the modern era, plus the famous sons and daughters, the industries, and the facts every resident should know.

title: Statehood
description: Maryland achieved statehood 1788 (7th). The road to statehood ran through territorial government, population thresholds, and a congressional enabling act — the standard American path. Civil War border state. Statehood Day is still celebrated, and the admission order gives Maryland its number among the states.

description: The statehood story of Maryland: settlement, territorial organization, the push for admission, and finally the star on the flag. Chesapeake Bay; federal workforce. Every state's admission reflected the national politics of its era — Maryland's story is no exception, and it explains much about the state's character today.

title: Capital: Annapolis
d: Annapolis is the capital of Maryland.
definition: Annapolis is the capital of Maryland.
description: Annapolis has been the seat of Maryland government, home to the capitol building, the supreme court, and the legislature. Capitals are often not the biggest city — Maryland's largest is Baltimore — chosen instead for geography or politics. Visit the capitol: the building itself tells the state's story in stone.

title: Nickname: Old Line State
d: Maryland is known as "Old Line State."
definition: Maryland is known as "Old Line State."
description: The nickname "Old Line State" captures how Maryland sees itself — and how America sees it. Fort McHenry's 1814 defense inspired the Star-Spangled Banner.
